signature.name: Jet d'Eau
signature.detail: Geneva's most famous symbol, a huge jet of water shooting high above the lake. It is free to view from the lakeshore and best seen on a clear day; walk along the Quai du Mont-Blanc or take a short boat ride for the classic photo.

signature.name: St. Pierre Cathedral
signature.detail: The city's main cathedral, known for its archaeology and its tower climb with sweeping views over the old town and lake. Go early to avoid crowds and note that the tower stairs are steep, so wear comfortable shoes.

signature.name: United Nations Office at Geneva
signature.detail: One of the world's key diplomatic sites, set in the Ariana park with the famous broken chair outside. Guided visits require booking ahead and a passport for security; check opening days before you go.

signature.name: Lake Geneva Tour
signature.detail: A boat trip on Lake Geneva is the best way to see the city from the water and reach the Jet d'Eau up close. Boats leave from the central piers; an hour-long cruise is an easy, scenic option.

signature.name: Reformation Wall
signature.detail: A dramatic monument in the Parc des Bastions honoring the leaders of the Reformation. It is free and open, a short walk from the old town, and pairs well with a stroll through the park.

signature.name: Jardin Anglais
signature.detail: A lakeside garden with the flower clock and views toward the Jet d'Eau. It is free and central, ideal for a short rest between the old town and the waterfront.

signature.name: Musée d'Art et d'Histoire
signature.detail: A large museum with fine art and archaeology, free for the permanent collection. It is a good rainy-day stop and a short walk from the old town.

signature.name: Téléphérique du Salève
signature.detail: A cable car up the Salève mountain for panoramic views over Geneva and the lake. Check operating days and weather before going, as it can close in poor conditions.

transport: Tram/bus about $3.5 a ride; day pass around $11
